newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian deputies rally against NATO expansion.
newsitem.headline: Russian deputies rally against NATO expansion.

text.p: Russian nationalist Sergei Baburin said on Friday he expected an overwhelming majority of parliamentary deputies to join a new group dedicated to safeguarding the country against NATO expansion to the east.

"The whole point of this group is to engage the attention not only of the public but of state structures, so that they take swift measures to protect the security...of all the Commonwealth of Independent States," he told a news conference.
Baburin said about 150 deputies had already signed up to the group and he expected a total of about 300 of about 450 members of the lower house of parliament to pledge support.
Signatories so far included representatives of the Communist Party, the Liberal Democrats of radical Vladimir Zhirinovsky, and the leftist Agrarians.
He said an eastward expansion, embracing such former allies as Poland and the Czech republic, could lead to the collapse of agreements on conventional and nuclear arms.
"Russia would have to review its military doctrine and its programme of arms," he said. But Baburin said he could not yet say precisely what measures the new group would take.

Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov is due to meet NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana on February 23 in Brussels for talks aimed at securing a deal over expansion. Talks on absorbing the first of Moscow's former Warsaw Pact allies are expected to begin later this year.
Baburin said Primakov had little to gain from talks.
"I wouldn't put great hopes on negotiations with Solana. Solana has an obligation to make promises but he doesn't have the right (powers) to carry out these promises," he said.

There is strong resistance to NATO expansion in the State Duma, which has so far failed to ratify the START-2 nuclear arms treaty. The Kremlin has made its opposition clear, but NATO officials are encouraged by signs Moscow remains ready to discuss the issue.
